title: Real-model Gateway route technical smoke
question: Can explicitly enabled technical real-model profiles traverse the frozen Gateway route while preserving bounded flow, frame integrity, cancellation, final flush, and generation-bound model selection?
hypothesis: A real-time-paced client that respects the advertised ingress credit can route full and partial worker batches without accepting malformed, non-finite, unnormalized, out-of-order, timestamp-mismatched, or stale output.

control.description: The same client state machine against a deterministic fake Gateway with delayed batches, partial flush, model switching, cancellation, and stale output injection.

variants.description: An authenticated disposable Gateway using at least two explicitly enabled technical model profiles and real-time-paced synthetic PCM.

environment.git_commit: Record the clean reviewed commit before a real run.
environment.runtime: Python 3.12 workspace lock, protocol v1, technical profiles explicitly enabled only on a loopback-bound single-session Gateway.
environment.hardware: Record server CPU, GPU, driver, CUDA, client host, browser, SSH path, and measured tunnel RTT for every real run.

model_revisions.profiles: Read exact profile, configuration, pack, evidence, endpoint, implementation, and weight digests from the supplied immutable registry.

procedure.summary: Validate the harness against deterministic faults, then route real-time-paced synthetic PCM through at least two technical profiles; verify catalog/session/worker identity, bounded credit, output headers and samples, partial end flush, stale cancellation exclusion, model switching, and explicit cleanup.
procedure.warmup: The technical smoke records cold readiness but does not use it as product latency evidence; any model-specific warmup is excluded from latency claims.
invalidation_conditions: The real Gateway does not use an exact reviewed commit, workspace lock, profile registry, model-pack digest, evidence digest, and installed worker wheel.
Fewer than two distinct profiles complete generation-bound selection and output validation.
The client exceeds the advertised ingress credit or accepts a stale, duplicate, reordered, timestamp-mismatched, non-finite, out-of-range, or unchanged output.
A trace contains raw PCM, bearer credentials, tickets, voice IDs, artifact paths, worker endpoints, model configuration values, or free-form server errors.
A technical pass is represented as a product, quality, speaker, Japanese-content, latency, authorization, license, or deployment-readiness decision.

decision_rule: The experiment decision is always inconclusive. A technical pass requires at least two distinct profiles, exact catalog/session/worker identity, no credit overrun, no malformed or stale accepted frame, finite normalized changed output, successful partial flush, generation-bound switching, bounded cancellation, and explicit session cleanup. It never advances voice quality, speaker identity, Japanese content, latency, license, authorization, security isolation, deployment, or production-readiness gates.

artifact_policy.raw_location: Raw synthetic PCM remains in process memory; optional technical traces are written only to an operator-selected path outside Git.
artifact_policy.git_contents: Harness source, schemas, deterministic fake fixtures, aggregate non-sensitive route results, and an inconclusive decision only.
artifact_policy.retention: Delete local traces after review or within 14 days; no raw audio is persisted by the harness.
artifact_policy.authorization: Only project-authored synthetic PCM and separately authorized target/model artifacts may be used. The trace never records target voice identifiers or artifact locations.
